limits: One run per reviewer per change, temperature 0 for Gemini and the default for claude -p. A second run could differ.
The ground truth is our own work: executed probes, X-Ray, Time Machine and regeneration results from runs/. It is not an independent list of every defect.
Whether a naive review 'mentions' a finding was judged by us. We leaned toward the naive reviewers (specific statements count, vague ones do not), but it is still our judgment.
The naive prompt is one choice. A longer prompt, repository access or tools would likely find more. We gave no tools, and claude -p had an empty working directory.
Only four changes from one repository, and these reviews saw the diff and the issue text only.
False and unverified counts only include what we could check by reading code or our own runs. 'Unverified' means plausible but not checked.

ground_truth.text: Hunk h4 (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull location helper) is unprotected: all 59 targeted tests pass when it is reverted.
The constructor filter drops a diagnostic that base reported: MsgPack004, twice with Location.None, for a closed generic class from a referenced assembly with an unkeyed member.

The code comment saying analyzers are not permitted to report against a location that does not exist overstates: base reported Location.None diagnostics without error.
The broad filter is not what fixes the crash (the FirstOrDefault change in h5 is); only the agent's UnkeyedMember test notices the filter, and it asserts the drop.

Two source groups are unprotected by the 13 new tests: the IsUserDeclaredFormatter equality line in ObjectSerializationInfo and the four new analyzer descriptors.

what_naive_review_lacks: Both naive reviews are prose with no executed check, no log and no file reference a person can open to confirm a statement, and both sound equally sure when they are right and when they are wrong. Receipts attaches a run, a log or a refusal to every statement, so the owner can check it.
